name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: Fitburg sabotage verdict; no new cut
summary: Finnish court convicts Fitburg crew over Baltic cable damage; no new cable cut found as of 11 Nov
state: A Helsinki court on 5 Nov convicted the Fitburg's Russian captain and an Azerbaijani crew member over damage to a Helsinki–Tallinn cable on 31 Dec 2025, jailing the captain (Euronews; Baird Maritime); the ruling can be appealed. Searches to 11 Nov found no new cable cut or major new GNSS jamming escalation. The ruling concerns a past incident, so Watch holds rather than rising.
for_you: Internet and telecoms users in the Baltic region are unlikely to notice effects, as operators reroute traffic around damaged cables. Air travel continues normally despite regional GPS interference.
rubric_hit: Cable damage incident (Fitburg sabotage conviction, 5 Nov) = Watch; no multiple cuts isolating a region for Alert

sources.title: Euronews — Finnish court jails Russian captain over Baltic Sea cable sabotage
Baird Maritime — Two cargo ship crew convicted in Finland for subsea cable sabotage

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
